environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed with custom runtime wrapper. The function executes inside a pivot_root'd mount namespace created by the bootstrap script before handler invocation. The confined root is a minimal tmpfs at /var/task/sandbox containing only the function code and node_modules. The process runs under a seccomp-bpf profile (applied via LD_PRELOAD libseccomp shim in the Lambda layer) that blocks syscalls: execve (except for /var/lang/bin/node itself via arg inspection), clone with CLONE_NEWNS, ptrace, and mount. Additionally, all environment variables except NODE_PATH and LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT are scrubbed by the bootstrap wrapper before the Node.js process starts — the IAM session credentials are never populated into the function's process environment (the execution role has sts:AssumeRole denied via an SCP on the OU, so even if credentials leaked they'd be unusable). The /proc filesystem is mounted with hidepid=2 and the process has no access to /proc/self/environ.
